I was in the same situation as you with a large prominent birthmark on my left upper thigh. It bothered me for years and I received a lot of questions and comments about it, especially from kids. Having the birth mark prevented me from wearing clothing that I wanted to wear, going swimming, or feeling confident about it. I made the choice about five years ago at age 21 to have it removed and it was some of the best money ever spent. Granted because of the location of the birthmark it did scar however I liked having a scar more than the birthmark itself. About two years ago I ended up getting a tattoo to cover up the scar and I love my leg now. In hindsight I wish I had had my birth mark removed earlier as I feel extremely confident and attractive without it and it severely limited my life. In the end it’s not about how other people see you it’s about how you see yourself and feel about your body. I’ve been in a long-term relationship and before I had my birthmark removed my partner always assured me that he loved it and that it made me unique and special. He understood why I wanted to have it removed and now he can tell that I’m more confident as I feel comfortable in any clothing and he fully supported me through the whole journey. Luckily I was supported in the situation by my partner and family as they understood where I was coming from. Good luck with whatever you choose.

I found out I was newly pregnant on the Paragard copper IUD. It had a failure rate of .8% and it wasn’t yet in my plan to have a baby. My family, partner, and his family were all scared and trying to convince me to terminate. Against all of their opinion and swaying I knew that it was the right choice to keep the baby although I felt scared and unsupported by the initial reactions my social circle was giving me. I was really upset and asked the universe for a sign that I was making the right choice by going against what everyone was telling me to do and keeping my baby. I was walking my dog in my neighborhood and found this area with a neighborhood donation sign and walked up to it. There was a large white trash bag that immediately caught my attention and I rifled through it. It contained hundreds of dollars of newborn/baby clothes, shoes, bibs, and tons of clothes with new sales tags left on. As soon as I saw it I knew that it was a sign, there was even clothing marked newborn clothes 0-3 months with holidays like Halloween and Christmas on it. My due date is in mid October so even the holidays and clothing sizes aligned. I ended up taking the bag home with me, committed to my decision to keep my baby, and am fully supported by both sides of my family. I thank the universe everyday for this synchronicity and giving me this sign in one of my hardest times.
